sections.title: A frontal figure with the sword tilted slightly aside
sections.bodyMarkdown:
The King sits facing us on a high-backed stone chair. A blue robe covers the legs, a purple cloak lies outside it and red appears at the neck and lining. The right hand holds a sword angled slightly toward the upper left, while the other rests beside the body. Above the crown, the chair’s back contains symmetrical carvings, including a clear butterfly shape.

Trees, clouds and blue sky flank the figure, with birds in the upper right. Compared with the Knight’s forward charge, this figure and chair form a stable central axis. Stability can support deliberation, but can also suggest a position reluctant to change. The image does not guarantee that a person in authority is correct. [View the image examined for this article](https://github.com/guangtoulee/destinypixel/blob/284f7641e41dcaa6685d2d387e31245ca8264d66/public/tarot/rws/king-of-swords.webp)

sections.title: Waite focuses on the power conferred by office
sections.bodyMarkdown:
In the transcription labelled 1911, Waite places the King in a position of judgment, connecting the card with authority, command and law. He notes its resemblance to the Major Arcana card Justice, while placing greater emphasis on the power granted by office. Reversal concerns harmful uses of that power.

This article develops a modern reading through evidence, procedure and accountability. It concerns everyday decision-making, not legal conclusions. Nor must the King correspond to a male manager, a father or someone in a particular profession. [Check Waite’s original entry](https://original.sacred-texts.com/tarot/pkt/pktswki.htm)

sections.title: Upright: Make the decision understandable to others
sections.bodyMarkdown:
Upright, the card can remind you to establish standards, compare facts and explain why you reached a decision. Different views need not be challenges to your position. Answering questions usually provides firmer grounds for trust than merely looking resolute.

Consistency does not mean mechanically treating different circumstances as identical. Explain why relevant differences matter; record the reason for an exception. Responsibility also includes acknowledging incomplete information and knowing when to involve someone with better knowledge.

sections.title: Reversed: Do the rules apply only to other people?
sections.bodyMarkdown: Reversed, the card can suggest choosing the verdict first and then finding reasons, or using technical language to prevent disagreement. You may demand exacting standards of others while leaving your own errors unexplained. Check whether standards are consistent, affected people can speak and mistakes have a path to correction.

sections.title: Leave room for review when a decision affects people
sections.bodyMarkdown:
When allocating team tasks, consider workload, skill and time rather than who objects least. Explaining your reasons makes omissions and unfairness easier to identify.

When selecting a collaborative proposal, establish the assessment criteria before reading the options so you are less likely to collect evidence only for the one you already like. In a household agreement about shared spending, discuss recordkeeping and exceptions. Being the person who keeps the accounts does not confer the final say.

sections.title: Practice: Write a short explanation of a decision
sections.bodyMarkdown: Choose a decision that affects someone else. State the standards used, the main evidence, what remains uncertain and who can add information. End with: “If ___ happens, I will reassess.” A judgment open to correction need not depend entirely on authority to sustain it.

sections.title: Reason is not permission to disregard feeling
sections.bodyMarkdown: The King of Swords does not equate professionalism with having no feelings and cannot guarantee that a ruling will favour you. The circumstances of affected people are relevant information too. Orderly thinking should clarify responsibility rather than make people harder to hear.

articleMarkdown:
# King of Swords Meaning: Give Reasons for Your Judgment

In one sentence: Having the authority to decide also means explaining your grounds and accepting review.

Keywords: Judgment · Standards · Responsibility

Upright at a glance: Decide using consistent standards and reliable facts, and take responsibility for the consequences.

Reversed at a glance: Authority may be overruling evidence, or rules may be concealing prejudice and control.

“Just do what I say” can end a discussion without producing a decision anyone has reason to trust.

## A frontal figure with the sword tilted slightly aside

The King sits facing us on a high-backed stone chair. A blue robe covers the legs, a purple cloak lies outside it and red appears at the neck and lining. The right hand holds a sword angled slightly toward the upper left, while the other rests beside the body. Above the crown, the chair’s back contains symmetrical carvings, including a clear butterfly shape.

Trees, clouds and blue sky flank the figure, with birds in the upper right. Compared with the Knight’s forward charge, this figure and chair form a stable central axis. Stability can support deliberation, but can also suggest a position reluctant to change. The image does not guarantee that a person in authority is correct. [View the image examined for this article](https://github.com/guangtoulee/destinypixel/blob/284f7641e41dcaa6685d2d387e31245ca8264d66/public/tarot/rws/king-of-swords.webp)

## Waite focuses on the power conferred by office

In the transcription labelled 1911, Waite places the King in a position of judgment, connecting the card with authority, command and law. He notes its resemblance to the Major Arcana card Justice, while placing greater emphasis on the power granted by office. Reversal concerns harmful uses of that power.

This article develops a modern reading through evidence, procedure and accountability. It concerns everyday decision-making, not legal conclusions. Nor must the King correspond to a male manager, a father or someone in a particular profession. [Check Waite’s original entry](https://original.sacred-texts.com/tarot/pkt/pktswki.htm)

## Upright: Make the decision understandable to others

Upright, the card can remind you to establish standards, compare facts and explain why you reached a decision. Different views need not be challenges to your position. Answering questions usually provides firmer grounds for trust than merely looking resolute.

Consistency does not mean mechanically treating different circumstances as identical. Explain why relevant differences matter; record the reason for an exception. Responsibility also includes acknowledging incomplete information and knowing when to involve someone with better knowledge.

## Reversed: Do the rules apply only to other people?

Reversed, the card can suggest choosing the verdict first and then finding reasons, or using technical language to prevent disagreement. You may demand exacting standards of others while leaving your own errors unexplained. Check whether standards are consistent, affected people can speak and mistakes have a path to correction.

## Leave room for review when a decision affects people

When allocating team tasks, consider workload, skill and time rather than who objects least. Explaining your reasons makes omissions and unfairness easier to identify.

When selecting a collaborative proposal, establish the assessment criteria before reading the options so you are less likely to collect evidence only for the one you already like. In a household agreement about shared spending, discuss recordkeeping and exceptions. Being the person who keeps the accounts does not confer the final say.

## Practice: Write a short explanation of a decision

Choose a decision that affects someone else. State the standards used, the main evidence, what remains uncertain and who can add information. End with: “If ___ happens, I will reassess.” A judgment open to correction need not depend entirely on authority to sustain it.

## Reason is not permission to disregard feeling

The King of Swords does not equate professionalism with having no feelings and cannot guarantee that a ruling will favour you. The circumstances of affected people are relevant information too. Orderly thinking should clarify responsibility rather than make people harder to hear.

## Read next

Justice: Compare weighing fairness with the decision-making responsibility of an office; Queen of Swords: Consider clear standards together with listening and boundaries.

sourceRecord.title: 宝剑国王牌义 为你的判断给出理由
sourceRecord.plainLanguageSummary: 有权作决定的人，也需要说明依据并接受复核。
sourceRecord.hook: 「就按我说的做」可以结束一次讨论，却未必构成一个值得信任的决定。
sourceRecord.uprightQuickTake: 用一致的标准和可靠事实作决定，并承担后果。
sourceRecord.reversedQuickTake: 权威压过证据，或用规则掩盖偏见和控制。

sections.title: 人物正面坐着 剑略向一侧倾斜
paragraphs: 国王正面坐在高背石椅上，蓝色长袍覆盖双腿，外披紫色披风，领部和内衬可见红色。右手握剑，剑身从胸前向画面左上方略微倾斜；另一只手停在身体侧旁。王冠上方的椅背布满对称雕纹，其中有清楚的蝴蝶形图案。

两边背景是树、云和蓝色天空，右上方有飞鸟。相较骑士的前冲，这里的人物和椅背形成稳定的中轴。稳定可以支持审慎，也可能令人联想到不易改变的位置；画面没有保证坐在高位者必然正确。 [查看本篇实看牌面](https://github.com/guangtoulee/destinypixel/blob/284f7641e41dcaa6685d2d387e31245ca8264d66/public/tarot/rws/king-of-swords.webp)

sections.title: Waite 更关心职位所拥有的裁决权
paragraphs: Waite 在1911年标注转录中把国王描述为处在裁决位置，联系判断、权威、命令和法律。他指出这张牌与大牌正义有相似处，同时更强调职位授予的权力。逆位着重于权力的不良运用。
本文由此延伸出证据、程序与问责的现代读法。这里谈的是日常决定如何作出，不提供法律结论；国王也不固定对应男性上司、父亲或某个特定职业。 [核对 Waite 单牌原文](https://original.sacred-texts.com/tarot/pkt/pktswki.htm)

sections.title: 正位 把判断变成别人能理解的过程
paragraphs: 正位可以提醒你先确定标准，再比较事实，最后说明为什么作出这个决定。若不同意见出现，不必把它们视作对地位的挑战；能回应质疑，通常比只维持坚定表情更可靠。
一致不等于所有情况机械地同样处理。条件确实不同，就说明差异为何相关；需要例外，就记录理由。对结果负责也包括承认信息不足，知道何时应请更了解情况的人参与。

sections.title: 逆位 规则有没有只约束别人
paragraphs: 逆位可提示先有结论再找理由，或借专业术语让人无法提出异议。也可能对别人十分严格，对自己的错误却不作说明。检查标准是否一致、受影响的人是否有机会陈述，以及出现错误后有没有修正路径。

sections.title: 在有影响的决定里多留一步复核
paragraphs: 团队分配任务时，先看工作量、技能与时间，而不是谁最少反对。把分配理由说明白，才容易看见遗漏和不公平。
挑选合作方案时，先列评估条件，再阅读各方案，避免只为已经喜欢的选项找证据。家庭约定共同开支，可以讨论记录方式与例外情况，不能把自己负责记账变成自己拥有最终决定权。

sections.title: 练习 给一个决定写简短说明
paragraphs: 选一个会影响别人的决定，写出采用的标准、主要依据、尚存的不确定，以及谁可以提出补充。最后加一句：「如果＿＿发生，我会重新评估。」能够被修正的判断，才不会只能靠权威撑住。

sections.title: 理性不是免除感受的通行证
paragraphs: 宝剑国王不代表没有感情才专业，也不能保证某项裁决必然对你有利。受影响者的处境同样是相关信息；有条理地思考，应让责任更清楚，而不是让人更难被听见。
